name: Segment Anything Medical Benchmark (SAM2 Medical Benchmark)
description: Recent advances in segmentation foundation models have enabled accurate and efficient segmentation across a wide range of natural images and videos, but their utility to medical data remains unclear. In this work, we first present a comprehensive benchmarking of the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) across 11 medical image modalities and videos and point out its strengths and weaknesses by comparing it to SAM1 and MedSAM. Then, we develop a transfer learning pipeline and demonstrate SAM2 can be quickly adapted to medical domain by fine-tuning. Furthermore, we implement SAM2 as a 3D slicer plugin and Gradio API for efficient 3D image and video segmentation. The code has been made publicly available at \url{https://github.com/bowang-lab/MedSAM}.
typical_sota_score: varies by modality; mean Dice commonly reported in the range ~60–95% depending on dataset and anatomy
reputation: A recent, focused benchmark evaluating SAM2 on medical modalities with growing interest from medical imaging researchers but not yet a community-wide standard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark. Performance varies widely across modalities and tasks; evaluation depends on available ground-truth masks (annotation variability). Includes transfer-learned and fine-tuned settings; potential domain shift and limited per-modality sample sizes for some modalities.
